title: Where things are: staan, zitten, liggen, hangen, lopen
intro: Dutch rarely says that something “is” somewhere. It says the thing stands, sits, lies or hangs there. The same verbs also make the Dutch way to say “I'm busy doing something”.

notes.title: 1. staan: things that stand upright
body: Things that stand upright, or on legs or wheels, staan: a bottle, a cup, a bike, a car, a house.
Words on paper or a screen also staan. Het staat in de app means “It's in the app.” Ik sta op de lijst means “I'm on the list.”

examples.en: The bike is in front of the door.
The milk is in the fridge.

examples.nl: Het [staat] in de app van school.

links.label: Wikibooks Dutch, lesson 9: staan, zitten, liggen, lopen

notes.title: 2. liggen: flat things, and places on a map
body: Things that lie flat liggen: a phone, keys, a book, a towel.
Towns and buildings also liggen. De sportschool ligt naast de supermarkt means “The gym is next to the supermarket.”

examples.en: Your phone is on the table.
The gym is next to the supermarket.

notes.title: 3. zitten: inside something, and clubs and classes
body: Things inside something that holds them, like a bag, a pocket or a box, zitten. People zitten when they sit.
Zitten op means taking part in a club or class: ze zit op zwemles. Zitten in tells you the school year: ze zit in groep drie.

examples.en: Your water bottle is in your bag.

notes.title: 4. hangen: things that hang
body: Coats, pictures and lamps hangen. So does a guitar on a hook on the wall.

examples.en: Your coat is on the coat rack.
My guitar is on the wall.

notes.title: 5. Busy doing something: zit te, staat te, ligt te, loopt te
body: To say what someone is doing right now, Dutch often uses zit, staat, ligt or loopt, then te and a verb at the end. Pick the one that matches the body position.
Ik zit te eten means “I'm eating” while sitting. Ze staat te wachten means “She's waiting” while standing.
If the position doesn't matter, use aan het: ik ben aan het koken.

links.label: Wikibooks Dutch, lesson 9: staan, zitten, liggen, lopen + te
Wikibooks Dutch, lesson 14: aan het and other ways to say “-ing”

notes.title: 6. lopen, rennen, hardlopen
body: Lopen means to walk. Rennen means to run fast, for example to catch the bus. Hardlopen is running as a sport, and it splits: ik loop hard.
Lopen also means that something is going or working. Hoe loopt het? means “How is it going?”

examples.en: I go running three times a week.

notes.title: 7. Changing position: ga zitten, ga staan, ga liggen
body: To sit down, stand up or lie down, use gaan with the position verb at the end. You hear these in every spin class.

examples.en: Go and lie down for a bit.

notes.title: 8. liggen or leggen? staan or zetten?
body: liggen says where something lies: ik lig, ze ligt. leggen is the action of putting something down flat: ik leg, ze legt. So it is ik lig te slapen, never ik leg te slapen.
For upright things, and things that go inside something, the action is zetten: ik zet de melk in de koelkast. For things that hang, it is hangen for both.

examples.en: I'm putting your phone on the table.

examples.nl: Ik [zet] de melk in de koelkast.
examples.en: I'm putting the milk in the fridge.

cards.nl: De fiets staat voor de deur.
cards.en: The bike is in front of the door.

cards.nl: De melk staat in de koelkast.
cards.en: The milk is in the fridge.

cards.nl: Het staat in de app van school.
Waar staat de auto?
Je telefoon ligt op tafel.
cards.en: Your phone is on the table.

cards.nl: Waar liggen mijn sleutels?
De sportschool ligt naast de supermarkt.
cards.en: The gym is next to the supermarket.

cards.nl: Je drinkfles zit in je tas.
cards.en: Your water bottle is in your bag.

cards.nl: Ze zit op taekwondo.
cards.rule: A club or class: zitten op.

cards.nl: Ze zit in groep drie.
Je jas hangt aan de kapstok.
cards.en: Your coat is on the coat rack.

cards.nl: Mijn gitaar hangt aan de muur.
cards.en: My guitar is on the wall.

cards.nl: Ik zit te werken.
cards.rule: Sitting and doing something: zit te + verb.

cards.nl: Ze staat bij het hek te wachten.
cards.rule: Standing and doing something: staat … te wachten.

cards.nl: Ze ligt al te slapen.
cards.rule: Lying down and doing something: ligt te + verb.

cards.nl: Ik ben aan het koken.
cards.rule: Position doesn't matter: ben aan het + verb.

cards.nl: Wat zit je te doen?
cards.rule: zit … te doen: what are you doing, sitting there?

cards.nl: We lopen elke dag naar school.
cards.en: We walk to school every day.
alts: Elke dag lopen we naar school.

cards.nl: Rennen, de bus komt eraan!
Hoe loopt het?
cards.rule: lopen can mean that something is going.

cards.nl: Ga maar zitten.
Ik lig te slapen.
cards.rule: liggen: ik lig. Ik leg means I put something down.

cards.nl: Ik leg je telefoon op tafel.
cards.en: I'm putting your phone on the table.

cards.nl: Ik zet de melk in de koelkast.
cards.en: I'm putting the milk in the fridge.

cards.nl: Leg je jas maar op de stoel.
cards.en: Just put your coat on the chair.
cards.rule: A coat lies flat on a chair: leggen.

cards.nl: Ga even liggen, je bent moe.
cards.en: Go and lie down for a bit, you're tired.
